title: Open Values Ask Core Index v0.1
description: The small search index the app loads at startup for Ask, the site's search box. It covers categories, brands, companies, labels, guides, errands and lines, but not single entries. The data build writes it, and the app reads it on every visit.

format.description: Names this file's format, so a reader can check it before reading the rest of the file.

version.description: The version of the format this file follows, such as "0.1".

built.description: The date of the source data this file was built from, as YYYY-MM-DD.

source.description: The files this index was built from, as paths in the repository.

strategy.description: A short note on how the index is meant to be used.

targetFields.description: The fields each record in targets carries.

startupContract.description: What the app can count on when it loads this index at startup: size, coverage, matching rules, and what to do when nothing matches.

tokens.description: A map from each normalized word or phrase to the ids it can find. The same as in ask-index.json, without entries (items), so it is small enough to load at startup.

aliases.description: A map from each normalized name to the one id it names exactly.

targets.description: A map from each id to its type, name and route, so results can be shown without loading other files.

stats.description: Counts by name, such as "tokens", "aliases", "targets", and the matching counts in the full index.

type.description: What the target is, such as "category", "brand", "company", "tag", "guide", "errand" or "line".

label.description: The target's name as shown to readers.

hash.description: The route of the target's page, such as "#n/brand/7up".

purpose.description: One sentence on what this contract is for.

appLaneNote.description: A note on which choices this contract leaves to the app.

loadHint.description: Always "eager-search": the app loads this file at startup.

budget.description: The startup size limit and how much room is left under it.

covers.description: Which kinds of target this index covers, and which it leaves to the full index.

resolver.description: The matching rules for queries against this index.

lazyBoundary.description: When and how to load the full index, ask-index.json.

emptyState.description: What to offer when a query finds nothing.

goldenQueries.description: Sample queries with the results this index gives for them, used to test the app.

maxBytes.description: The startup size limit in bytes.

currentBytes.description: The size of ask-core.json in bytes.

minimumHeadroomBytes.description: How many bytes must stay free under the limit.

withinBudget.description: True when currentBytes is not more than maxBytes.

hasMinimumHeadroom.description: True when headroomBytes is at least minimumHeadroomBytes.

measurement.description: How the size is measured, such as UTF-8 bytes.

layer.description: Always "core", the startup layer of Ask.

targetTypes.description: The kinds of target this index covers.

deferredTargetTypes.description: The kinds of target left to the full index, such as "item".

targetFields.description: The fields each target record carries.

normalization.description: How query text is changed before matching, such as lowercasing and removing accents and punctuation.

stopWords.description: Words dropped from queries before matching, such as "is", "best" and "bad".

rankOrder.description: The match reasons from strongest to weakest, with type as the tiebreak.

maxStartupResults.description: The most results to show from this index.

use.description: What the full index is for.

trigger.description: What should cause the app to load the full index.

keepCoreIfLazyFails.description: Always true: if the full index fails to load, startup search keeps working.

failureMode.description: What the app should do when the full index fails to load.

primary.description: The route of the main thing to offer, such as a request for the missing item.

secondary.description: The route of the second thing to offer, such as browsing.

mustNot.description: What the app must not do when nothing matches.

query.description: The query as a person would type it.

normalized.description: The query after normalization and stop-word removal.

intent.description: What the person is after, in a few words, such as "company/brand concern".

expectAny.description: At least one of these ids must come back.

expectOneInTop.description: One expected id must rank within this many results.

matched.description: The id of the highest-ranked result that is in expectAny.

matchedRank.description: The rank of that result, counting from 1.

expectFirstHash.description: The route of the first result.

expectMatchedHash.description: The route of the matched result.

ok.description: Always true in a valid file: the matched result ranks within expectOneInTop and every ordering check passed.

top.description: The top results for the query, in rank order.

label.description: The result's name as shown to readers.

type.description: What the result is, such as "brand" or "company".

hash.description: The route of the result's page.

score.description: The match score; a higher score ranks first. Alias matches score 120, exact 110, a query word 95, one letter off 86, and overlapping words 76 less the difference in word count.

reason.description: The rule that produced the match: "alias" (an exact name), "exact" (an exact word or phrase), "query-token" (one word of the query), "fuzzy-1" (one letter off) or "token-containment" (the words overlap).

key.description: The word or phrase in the index that the query matched.
